newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent touches new low on Iraq, U.S. gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent touches new low on Iraq, U.S. gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude on Wednesday touched new session lows shortly after the U.S. open, extending early losses posted after Iraq said it was expecting to resume crude exports by the middle of August.
Sept Brent touched a low of $19.23 a barrel before recovering slightly to trade at $19.30 by 1420 GMT, 22 cents below Tuesday's close.
Losses on U.S. gasoline were giving the early slide added momentum, brokers said.
"Gasoline came off quite quickly and that is adding to the Iraqi impact," said one.
Oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said on Wednesday Iraq expected to export the full $2 billion worth of oil allowed under the U.N. oil-for-food plan before the December 6 deadline.

The second phase of the deal began on June 8 but Iraq's insistence on a revised aid distribution plan delayed the restart and means it will have to export flat out to meet the interim $1 billion target by the September 5 deadline.
Rasheed said Iraq was capable of producing 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and exporting 1.8 million bpd.
Traders were trying to contact Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation on Wednesday to agree new contract volumes.
NYMEX Sept gasoline touched a low of 65.70 cents a gallon but recovered by 1451 GMT to trade at 66.70 cents, down 0.40 cents.

Dealers said a three million barrel fall in U.S. gasoline inventories last week, reported by the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Department of Energy (DOE) had been expected and was already reflected in the price.
"If anything the DOE figures were slightly more constructive (for gasoline) but the market is looking softer," said one.
Meanwhile, IPE Aug gas oil shed $1.00 to $175.25 a tonne by 1451 GMT. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
